feasibility_reason: The TUH EEG Slowing dataset is a well-known public clinical EEG dataset from Temple University Hospital. Despite the analysis.md excerpt being empty and references being mostly irrelevant or misattributed (the one partial reference conflates it with TUSZ seizure corpus), this dataset is specifically designed for detecting pathological slowing patterns in EEG, supporting binary or multi-class classification of abnormal vs. normal EEG slowing activity.

event_annotations.notes: No raw event IDs were detected in the dataset (explicitly stated as '(no events detected)' in the input). The TUH EEG Slowing Corpus v2.0.1 AAREADME.txt describes three clinical phenomena present in sessions (seizure events, slowing events, complex background events), but these are not event markers or trigger codes—they are clinical annotations/labels assigned to continuous EEG segments via separate .tse/.tse_bi annotation files. No events.tsv, events.json, EDF annotations, or other event channel data was accessible despite exhaustive attempts across multiple patient/session directories using standard TUH naming conventions (.edf, .rec, .tse, .tse_bi, .lbl, .csv, .tsv, .json with various prefix/suffix combinations). Without detectable raw event IDs from embedded EDF event channels or sidecar files, no event annotations can be assigned.
